paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: God finishes what He starts. The One on the throne says, "Behold, I make all things new," and then He says, "It is done!" (Revelation 21:5-6). Everything broken, tearful and worn down gets made new. I know a little about being worn down, baker, and I have seen what He does with it.

Look at WHO is in the middle of the new city. No temple, because "the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple" (Revelation 21:22). "The dwelling place of God is with man" (Revelation 21:3), and His servants "will see His face" (Revelation 22:4). That is the best part, baker. It is not the gold streets or the pearl gates, it is being home with Him, with every tear wiped away and no curse left anywhere (Revelation 21:4; 22:3).

The invitation is open, too. He gives freely from the spring of the water of life "To the thirsty" (Revelation 21:6), and the city is for those "whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life" (Revelation 21:27). So hold on, friend, and keep your ovens ready. The Lamb is Jesus, His Supper is the one I'm baking for, and the best is still coming.
